title: Jensen Huang Reportedly Wants Back In As Nvidia CEO. How Will Stock React?
detail:
Jensen Huang Reportedly Wants Back In As Nvidia CEO. How Will Stock React?
Lockridge Okoth
Sun, November 15, 2026 at 2:23 PM EST 2 min read
NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on Thursday. Three days later, he is reportedly talking about coming back.

Huang has discussed a return with confidants, the Financial Times reported Sunday, citing several people familiar with the matter. One ally is building a "war room" of tech executives to lobby the board and the White House.

Why Huang Left Nvidia

Huang stepped down after reports of affairs with a subordinate and with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. The FT describes her as a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has put Nvidia's sudden leadership crisis under a spotlight, along with how it sells AI chips to Asian buyers with possible China links.

Even his supporters admit the problem. "Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence," one person working on his return told the FT.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress now runs Nvidia on an interim basis. The FT also reported the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor. Nvidia said no "formal" process has started.

Silicon Valley Versus Washington

"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," that ally told the FT. Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney backed a public letter urging the board to "Bring Jensen Back."

Washington is pushing the other way. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shake-up" in Nvidia's leadership.

Huang never held a controlling stake. As BeInCrypto reported, only Nvidia's board decides whether he returns.

How Will Nvidia Stock React?

Big investors are split. Billionaire Leo KoGuan told Bloomberg he has stopped buying.

"No further investment without Jensen," he said.

Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker, both large shareholders, asked the board to keep "all options on the table," including Huang's return.

Shares closed down 4.34% at $166.19 the day Huang quit, after falling as much as 14% intraday. They slipped again Friday. The stock sits more than 30% below its October 6 record and trades near 12 times expected earnings, its cheapest level since 2012. Bernstein cut its price target to $200 from $400.

Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Performance. Source: Yahoo Finance

Meanwhile, rival AMD has outrun Nvidia by a record margin. Tuesday's report, in a crowded week for AI stocks, will be Kress's first. Who leads Nvidia next is still undecided.

"It's going to be an interesting week to say the least," analysts at the Kobeissi Letter indicated.

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) is retaining most of its gains this year despite significant economic volatility and political change. Excitement about artificial intelligence (AI) and confidence in the economy are strong growth drivers, and the market has been rallying after a post-election drop.

But not every stock is enjoying a strong run this year. And while stocks that drop can scare investors, that's where you can often find the best opportunities. Dutch Bros (NYSE:BROS), MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI), and On Holding (NYSE:ONON) are all plunging this year, but they have fantastic long-term potential.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's why these three stocks could be great additions to your portfolio.

Image source: Dutch Bros.

1. Dutch Bros: Down 43%

Dutch Bros is a small coffee shop chain with big ambitions. It has created a unique model with exclusive customer beverages and a store portfolio that's mostly drive-thrus, and it has attracted a large customer base that keeps coming back for more.

Part of the company's success comes from its menu, which leans toward the sweet and cold, setting it apart from the classic coffee shop. People also love its friendly customer service and focus on speed.

Management has been at the forefront of beverage innovation, including being the first major chain to offer boba when it became popular two years ago and launching its own line of Myst healthy energy drinks.

Revenue increased 30% year over year in the third quarter, and same-shop sales were up 4.4%. Net income increased from $27.3 million to $37.2 million.

Dutch Bros has 1,273 locations as of the end of the third quarter, and management says it has visibility to reach its goal of 2,029 stores by 2029. That's nearly double today's count, which could lead to doubling revenue over the next four or so years from new stores alone.

The market, however, was disappointed by the lowered full-year guidance. Management is navigating inflation and higher costs, which are impacting the business from top to bottom.

However, the long-term outlook is very strong, and Dutch Bros should reward shareholders who hold for the long term.

2. MercadoLibre: Down 25%

MercadoLibre operates the largest e-commerce business in Latin America as well as a thriving financial platform, including what it expects to become the largest digital bank in Mexico.

Boeing Is Handing 3 Businesses to Archer Aviation and Closing a $131 Billion F-15 Order. Here’s Which Stock Gets the Better Deal.

Boeing (NYSE:BA) is selling three aerospace businesses to Archer Aviation (NYSE:ACHR), giving the electric aircraft developer an established defense operation generating more than $200 million in annual revenue. Meanwhile, Boeing has secured a U.S. military contract with a maximum value of $131.23 billion to support its F-15 fighter jet program.

Both developments could significantly improve the companies' long-term prospects. But they represent very different opportunities. Archer is gaining revenue, technology, and a stronger foothold in defense. Boeing is strengthening an already substantial military business while simplifying its operations.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

And while both deals look promising, one stock offers a more compelling opportunity. Let's find out which one.

Archer is getting three established aerospace businesses

In August, Boeing agreed to sell Archer three subsidiaries: Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid. Each brings something different.

Wisk develops autonomous electric aircraft capable of taking off and landing vertically, similar to helicopters. Its technology could eventually help Archer develop air taxis that operate without pilots. SkyGrid develops software for managing air traffic, including coordinating autonomous aircraft and drones.

But Insitu is arguably the most valuable addition. That company manufactures military drones used for intelligence gathering, surveillance, and reconnaissance. Unlike Archer's emerging air taxi business, Insitu already generates revenue and operates profitably.

Image source: Getty Images.

According to Boeing, Insitu produces more than $200 million in annual revenue and operates across 35 countries. That's a substantial addition for Archer, which generated just $5.1 million in revenue during Q3 2026. The acquisition could also help Archer expand its defense business beyond the electric air taxis that originally attracted investors.

Archer is already developing autonomous aircraft with defense technology company Anduril. Its Halo and Thunder platforms are intended for commercial and military applications, respectively. Adding Insitu's manufacturing experience, customer relationships, and established drone business could accelerate those efforts.

Boeing isn't giving these businesses away

Boeing isn't receiving cash for the three subsidiaries. Instead, it will receive newly issued Archer shares equal to approximately 19.75% of Archer's pre-transaction Class A share count, plus warrants that could allow it to acquire additional shares. Boeing will also retain access to Wisk's autonomous flight technology through a collaboration agreement.

Nvidia Corp's next earnings call will be about much more than another record quarter. For the first time in 33 years, Jensen Huang will not be at the helm when the company reports its third-quarter results. Interim CEO Colette Kress now faces the task of convincing investors that Nvidia's extraordinary AI growth can continue without the founder who built its dominance.

Here are five things investors need to hear on Nov. 17 when Nvidia's third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call takes place.

Don't Miss:

Investing in Real Estate Doesn't Have to Mean Buying a House. Here Are 4 Ways to Get Started

Credit Card Debt Is Getting Harder to Shake. 4 Steps to Take Before Your Balance Gets Even Bigger

1. Can Nvidia Deliver Despite Supply Constraints?

Supply remains one of Nvidia's biggest opportunities and risks. In its August earnings call, Kress said the company had increased its total supply, including inventory purchase commitments and prepayments, to $145 billion.

She acknowledged that Nvidia was not immune to supply challenges but expressed confidence in its ability to support customer demand.

Investors will want an update on whether suppliers can keep pace with demand and whether Nvidia can convert its massive order pipeline into revenue without further bottlenecks.

2. How Much More Will Memory Costs Pressure Margins?

Nvidia reported a non-GAAP gross margin of 75% in its second quarter and expected margins to remain in the mid-70% range for fiscal 2027.

But memory costs are becoming an important variable. Kress noted that consumer demand had fallen modestly amid higher memory and system prices.

Investors need to understand whether rising component costs are beginning to affect Nvidia's own profitability, particularly as the company moves toward increasingly complex AI systems.

3. Is Vera Rubin Still on Track for a Fast Ramp?

Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin platform is central to its growth beyond Blackwell. Kress said production shipments were expected to begin in the second half of 2026, starting in the third quarter, with the ramp continuing into the fourth quarter and first quarter of next year.

She cautioned that assembling the complex systems would take time, despite strong customer demand and purchase orders.

Investors will want confirmation that the transition is proceeding smoothly and that customers are prepared to deploy the new architecture at scale.
